name: Nuclear plant safety
value: ZNPP off-site power lost and restored 8 Nov
summary: Zaporizhzhia lost all off-site power on 8 Nov for the 27th time in the war; no safety-system damage reported
state: Zaporizhzhia lost its off-site power on 8 Nov when the Ferosplavna line disconnected, and ran on backup diesel generators until power was restored hours later; the IAEA said the cause and location of the fault were unknown and counted it as the 27th loss of off-site power in the war (ThePrint, citing Reuters). The main Dniprovska line remained unavailable as of 23 Oct. Searches on 14 Nov found no damage to safety-critical systems, INES level 2 event or radiological release.
for_you: There is no radiological risk to the public reported. Repeated power losses reduce safety margins at the plant; the IAEA publishes regular updates on conditions there.
rubric_hit: Watch: ZNPP lost all off-site power on 8 Nov; no safety-system damage or INES 2+ event

why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.
